# Cryptographic Prime Generation Using Miller-Rabin

## Objective

To generate a probable prime of 512-bit length using
the Miller-Rabin primality test.

## Theory

Miller-Rabin is a probabilistic primality testing algorithm.
It determines whether a given number is composite or probably prime.

The algorithm decomposes n-1 into 2^s * d, where d is odd.
It selects random bases and performs modular exponentiation.
If a candidate fails any round, it is rejected.
A candidate passing all rounds is considered a probable prime.

## Implementation

Language: Python

Bit Length: 512

Miller-Rabin Rounds: 20

Independent Verification: SymPy isprime()

## Execution

python3 modern/miller_rabin_prime_generation/src/generate_prime.py
